summary: Iteration 2 full-stack regression completed. Backend: 23/26 pytest checks passed; PDF generation, photo lifecycle, signature persistence, WhatsApp/public approval, reminders, external payments, admin payment mutation/deletion, service-order totals/adjustments, and hard/soft deletion passed. Frontend: WhatsApp/public approval, photo upload, signature (after dependency fix), order editing/add-part, reminders, and external-payment creation passed; PDF buttons download rather than open a tab, and a runtime overlay blocks payment edit/delete.

critical.issue: Non-admin technician receives 200 and can replace items, totals, and status; endpoint uses get_current_user instead of require_role('admin').
Accepts amount=-10 and persists a negative payment even though creation enforces amount > 0; this can corrupt collection totals and linked paid_total.

Public ingress answers trusted and untrusted preflights with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * instead of the explicit frontend origin. This occurs despite FastAPI code using FRONTEND_URL, indicating ingress-level CORS override/termination.

ui_bugs.issue: Kabul PDF and Teslim PDF both trigger attachment downloads rather than opening PDF tabs. Buttons are inside target=_blank anchors, but the backend sends Content-Disposition: attachment.

After creating an external payment, the webpack dev-server full-screen runtime overlay reports repeated 'ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications' errors and intercepts pointer events, making pencil/trash actions unclickable. Removing the overlay diagnostically makes edit open, confirming the underlying button works.

integration_issues.issue: Create succeeds and shows Harici/500, but normal edit and delete cannot be completed because the runtime error overlay obstructs the controls.

issues: Radix warns that DialogContent has no Description/aria-describedby on WhatsApp and payment dialogs, reducing screen-reader context.

action_items: Protect PUT /api/service-orders/{id} with require_role('admin') and rerun RBAC plus edit persistence tests.
Validate PaymentUpdate.amount as strictly positive before changing payment, transaction, or paid_total.
Change PDF response disposition to inline (or fetch a Blob and open its object URL) so both PDF actions open a new tab as specified.
Resolve the ResizeObserver runtime error or configure the dev-server overlay to ignore only the known benign ResizeObserver messages; verify payment edit/delete with normal clicks afterward.
Fix ingress CORS so credentialed cross-origin requests use only explicit trusted origins; do not return wildcard origin.
Reconcile inventory when service-order items are added, removed, or quantity changes, ideally in a transaction with order and ledger updates.
Retest all three failing backend checks and both blocked frontend flows.
critical_code_review_comments: update_service_order is documented/admin-presented as admin-only but authorizes every authenticated role.
PaymentUpdate has no positivity constraint; update_payment applies negative values directly to payment transactions and linked paid_total.
Service-order item edits recompute financial totals but never decrement stock for added parts, restore stock for removed parts, or apply quantity deltas.
storage_utils uses blocking requests calls inside async FastAPI endpoints, which can block the event loop for up to 120 seconds during object-storage operations.
Hard-deleting a service order does not delete or soft-delete its file_refs, so previously uploaded photos can remain authorized/downloadable and orphaned after the order is gone.
Approval tokens have no expiry or revocation metadata; links remain usable indefinitely until a decision is made.
server.py exceeds 1,200 lines and combines auth, data models, storage, PDF, approval, reporting, CRUD, and seeding; split into routers/services.
Frontend data loaders such as ServiceOrderDetail and Reminders do not render an API error state; failures can leave loading or empty content without actionable feedback.

success_rate.frontend: 70% of the 10 explicitly requested UI checks passed; additional photo, signature, and public approval checks passed

seed_data_creation: Created isolated TEST_I2/TEST_UI customers, motorcycles, service orders, users, photos, signatures, approval decisions, and payments. API fixture teardown plus cleanup_test_data.py removed test DB records; uploaded object bytes may remain physically in object storage because the product only soft-deletes file references.
test_credentials: Used admin credentials from /app/memory/test_credentials.md successfully. bcrypt $2b$, HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=None cookie, brute-force lockout after five failures, and seed password-update code all verified. /app/auth_testing.md is absent.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Final pytest is stable at 23 passed/3 failed: explicit-origin public CORS, non-admin service-order edit, and negative payment update. Signature initially failed with react-signature-canvas 1.1.0-alpha.2 (trim_canvas is not a function); dependency was pinned to 1.0.7, frontend restarted/built, and signature drawing/save then passed. PDF clicks were diagnosed with Playwright download events. Payment creation passes, but edit/delete normal clicks are reproducibly blocked by #webpack-dev-server-client-overlay after ResizeObserver runtime errors.
rca_of_the_issue: RBAC failure is caused by Depends(get_current_user) on update_service_order instead of require_role('admin'). Negative payments are caused by unconstrained Optional[float] in PaymentUpdate and no update-time invariant check. PDF behavior is caused by Content-Disposition: attachment. The payment obstruction is caused by webpack-dev-server surfacing ResizeObserver loop notifications as a full-screen iframe overlay. Public CORS wildcard responses appear to be emitted at ingress (204 with wildcard for both trusted and untrusted origins) before FastAPI's explicit-origin middleware handles preflight.
